page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-512 is an arm64 compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor platform. The server provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at a clock frequency of 3.6 GHz. Because the architecture assigns a single thread per core with dedicated CPU allocation, all 64 vCPUs operate as independent physical execution cores without hyperthreading resource sharing.

The instance is equipped with 512 GB of total system memory, providing an 8 GB per core memory footprint. The VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-512 contains no integrated local storage, requiring the use of remote block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators and comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In terms of hardware balance, the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides substantial memory density per core on an ARM-based compute architecture. This profile allows organizations running memory-bound systems to minimize unnecessary compute core count. A primary tradeoff is the complete reliance on network-attached storage due to the absence of bundled local NVMe drives.

Workloads aligned with this server profile include large-scale in-memory databases, distributed memory caching nodes, data transformation processes, enterprise microservices with high memory requirements, and ARM64-targeted software compilation pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-512 is an arm64 virtual machine instance powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. Operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz, the instance delivers 64 physical cores with dedicated allocation and a single thread per core, removing hyperthreading resource contention. The configuration includes 512 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to an 8 GB per core allocation ratio. It does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block volumes for persistent data, and features no dedicated GPU accelerators. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address. The generous memory-to-core allocation profile makes this instance cost-effective for resource-dense setups that require substantial memory capacity per thread without paying for specialized accelerator hardware. It is suited for in-memory databases, memory-bound caching systems, distributed data processing, enterprise backend services, and large-scale ARM-native application deployments.
